title: Module 6 quiz — WebSphere Liberty Modernization
description: Eight questions on ND vs Liberty, server.xml, compatibility, externalized config, and BayPay migration waves. Synthetic only.

questions.prompt: What is the best one-line contrast between BayPayCell and a Liberty payment server?
choices: Liberty cannot do JDBC; ND cannot do HTTP
ND is a managed cell (DMGR, node agents, synchronized nodes); Liberty is a process configured by server.xml and features you enable
Liberty requires a deployment manager; ND does not
They are identical operations models with different logos
questions.explanation: Traditional ND adds a management plane. Liberty enables Jakarta features in server.xml and is container-friendly. Both can serve a WAR; the operations model is the migration.

questions.prompt: A Liberty server.xml for payment-service.war omits jdbc-4.3 and jndi-1.0 but includes servlet-6.0. What fails first?
choices: The JVM cannot start at all
HTTP works; lookup of jdbc/baypay-payment fails because the JDBC/JNDI features were not enabled
SIBus BayPayBus starts automatically anyway
LTPA tokens are minted without a user registry
questions.explanation: Liberty is feature-gated. Servlet alone does not give you a DataSource or JNDI. Enable jdbc-4.3 and jndi-1.0 (and persistence-3.1 if you use JPA in the WAR).

questions.prompt: On Liberty, why should payment use jdbc/baypay-payment instead of the historical cell-wide jdbc/baypay?
choices: Liberty forbids the string baypay
So payment and refund (and reporting) do not share one pool and one outage
JNDI names cannot contain a hyphen
The Spring Boot reference app cannot run if any JNDI name exists
questions.explanation: Isolation is the point of the move. Re-creating one shared bind on Liberty copies the INCIDENT-503 failure domain into the target runtime.

questions.prompt: A compatibility assessment finds payment.ear still compiled against javax.servlet and a SIBus-only MDB. What is the honest classification?
choices: Lift-and-shift this weekend; Liberty is a drop-in ND
Package-rename may be mechanical; the SIBus MDB is rewrite or defer — not a silent lift
Delete the ear and tell finance to use spreadsheets
Keep ND forever because jakarta packages are illegal
questions.explanation: javax→jakarta is a known, often toolable change. SIBus is an ND-centric messaging fabric. Treat it as rewrite (JMS on a broker, or in-process events like the Boot app) or defer that ear.

questions.prompt: Which server.xml fragment is acceptable for BayPay production secrets?
choices: <properties.postgresql password="changeme-baypay"/>
<properties.postgresql password="${env.BAYPAY_DB_PASSWORD}"/> plus the value in server.env / a secret store, not in git
Put the password in featureManager
Hard-code the J2C alias baypayDbAlias inside the WAR
questions.explanation: Externalize like BAYPAY_DB_* on the Boot app. server.xml in git must not contain the live password. server.env or the platform secret injector supplies it.

questions.prompt: Why is Wave 1 on BayPay refund, not payment?
choices: RefundCluster has no database
Refund is lower volume and a smaller blast radius; payment stays on ND until the Liberty path is proven
Liberty cannot host a payment WAR
IHS cannot route to more than one cluster
questions.explanation: Wave 1 is a learning and rollback rehearsal. Payment is the money path. Prove features, DataSource isolation, and ops on refund first (TOPOLOGY waves).

questions.prompt: Wave 2 puts one Liberty payment replica behind ihs-east. Liberty p99 is 4× ND and error rate climbs. What is the rollback?
choices: Install a new traditional ND cell in AWS
Drain the canary; send 100% of payment traffic back to PaymentCluster; keep the Liberty config for a fix
Stop Pay1, Pay2, and Pay3 so Liberty is forced to win
Raise jdbc/baypay maxConnections on the cell to 500
questions.explanation: Rollback is a traffic move, not a platform tantrum. The ND cluster is the safety net until Wave 3. Do not grow maxConnections to hide a Liberty defect.

questions.prompt: When is Spring Boot the better BayPay target than a Liberty WAR this quarter?
choices: Never; this course forbids Boot after Module 3
New modules and the teaching reference app; Liberty when an ear must remain an ear on a short timeline
Only when you need SIBus
Only when you need a DMGR
questions.explanation: reference-apps/baypay stays Boot. Liberty is the ear-compatible modernization path. Neither choice is ‘put it on a new ND cell.’
